newsitem.title: USA: Scorching U.S. debut for Deutsche Telekom.
newsitem.headline: Scorching U.S. debut for Deutsche Telekom.

text.p: Deutsche Telekom AG made a scorching debut in New York trading, soaring around 14 percent to close 2-39/64 above Sunday's pricing at $21-1/2 on massive volume of 17 million shares.
The stock, part of a $13 billion global share offering in the company's first stage of privatization, eased from a high of 22-1/8 reached just minutes after opening.

The nominal U.S. pricing was $18-59/64, based on the exchange rate for the 28.5 mark issue price, but no trades took place anywhere near this level on Monday as the stock roared off in New York Stock Exchange trading.
Val Kosmider, head of international equity trading for Schroder Wertheim, noted traders had seen gains of $3 to $4 a share on overnight purchases of the stock.
"They are just saying, 'Hey, thank you very much," and moving on to the next thing," he said. "You're going to see very active trading for some time to come."

Five times oversubscribed, the offering could have been taken up by German demand alone. The 13-18 percent slice of the pie reserved for U.S. investors went well, despite some intial misgivings about the value the stock represented.

However, a pricing at 28.5 marks, well short of the top of the range 25-30 mark range was surprisingly conservative in view of euphoria about oversubscription ahead of the weekend pricing, and leaves some room for solid demand in the aftermarket, analysts said.

Nicholas Bratt, a managing director of the mutual fund firm Scudder, Stevens & Clark, described the initial public offering as a watershed event, and said the stock should trade higher over the next few weeks.
"It's very important for the Germans to have a success here," Bratt told reporters in Boston. -- New York Newsroom 212 859 1610
